scope.mapping_meaning: mapped_to_bounded_sticky_primitive means that the upstream question may be re-expressed through the named person-bounded sticky-noise primitive. It never authorizes the literal upstream SQL, its output schema, or direct execution.

privacy_contract.longitudinal_rule: Repeated OMOP records are reduced per person, de-duplicated as person/category pairs, or deterministically retained up to a public person-level cap k before aggregation.
privacy_contract.domain_rule: Every grouping domain, threshold, concept set, time interval and category order is public and fixed before data access; observed levels, data-dependent top-N values and data-dependent bins are forbidden.
privacy_contract.mechanism_rule: The mapping requires a dedicated server-owned fixed per-release sticky-noise mechanism with canonical semantic query identity. Deterministic disclosure control and nfilter.noise do not implement this mechanism. The registry selects reviewed algorithms; it is not a query quota or cumulative privacy budget.
privacy_contract.postprocessing_rule: Only noisy primitive outputs and deterministic post-processing of those outputs may be released; exact support checks, exact extrema and exact intermediate counts are not released.

families.contract: Evaluate one public predicate per person and count each qualifying person once, regardless of the number of matching OMOP records.
families.fixed_public_domain: The cohort predicate, concept sets, thresholds and temporal window are fixed and public before evaluation.

sensitivity.reason: Adding or removing one person changes one bounded Boolean contribution.

families.contract: De-duplicate person/category pairs, retain at most k categories per person using the primitive's deterministic public ordering, and emit every category in the declared domain, including zero-observation categories.
families.fixed_public_domain: The complete ordered category set and k are fixed and public; observed-only levels and data-dependent top-N selection are forbidden.

sensitivity.reason: Adding or removing one person changes at most k histogram cells by one.

families.contract: Count at most k records for each person and sum those bounded person contributions.
families.fixed_public_domain: The cohort, event predicate, temporal window and contribution cap k are fixed and public before evaluation.

sensitivity.reason: Adding or removing one person changes the bounded scalar record count by at most k.

families.contract: Retain at most k records per person using a declared ordering column and canonical category tie-break, then emit every category in the fixed domain, including zero-observation categories.
families.fixed_public_domain: The complete category or canonical tuple domain, record ordering and contribution cap k are fixed and public before evaluation.

sensitivity.reason: Adding or removing one person changes at most k total histogram contributions.

families.contract: De-duplicate categories within each person, retain at most k categories using canonical UTF-8 value ordering, and release the noisy cardinality of their union.
families.fixed_public_domain: The complete vocabulary-derived category domain and contribution cap k are fixed and public; protected values never define the release domain or ordering.

sensitivity.reason: Adding or removing one person can add or remove at most k categories from the union.

families.contract: Collapse longitudinal records to one public denominator Boolean and one public numerator Boolean per person, release both bounded counts with separate noise allocations, and derive the rate only as post-processing.
families.fixed_public_domain: Eligibility, index-event, outcome and follow-up definitions are fixed and public before evaluation.

sensitivity.reason: One person changes the denominator by at most one and the numerator by at most one; the two releases compose sequentially.

families.contract: Reduce to one numeric/date value per person or retain at most k deterministically ordered records per person, clip into fixed public breaks, and emit every public bin.
families.fixed_public_domain: Breaks, reducer, record order and any contribution cap k are fixed and public before evaluation.

sensitivity.reason: A person changes one bin after person reduction, or at most k bins under the explicitly capped records reducer.

families.contract: Reduce longitudinal values to one value per person, clip it to fixed public bounds and release only the bounded count and quantized sum used to derive the mean.
families.fixed_public_domain: Numeric bounds, reducer and quantization contract are fixed and public before evaluation.

sensitivity.reason: One person changes the bounded count by one and the quantized sum by at most the fixed server grid.

redesigns.public_domain: Controller-published comorbidity concept set and deterministic per-person category cap k.
Controller-published condition concept set and deterministic per-person category cap k.
Public index-condition, eligibility, follow-up and death definitions.
Controller-published indication concept set and deterministic per-person category cap k.
Public drug and contraindication concept predicates.
Public observation-period duration predicate of more than 365 days.
Public calendar year and continuous-observation predicate.
The complete ordered month domain 1 through 12; exact birth dates and years remain unavailable.

executable_catalog.input_contract: Each mapping operates only on a server-created person-local omop.table prepared through the typed Recipe/Plan path. The mapping fixes the sticky primitive and longitudinal reducer; the analyst must supply every public domain, bound, bin, concept set, time window and record cap before data access.
executable_catalog.output_contract: Only the sticky primitive output and deterministic post-processing may leave the server. Exact support branches, observed categories, data-dependent top-N values, raw extrema and intermediate rows are forbidden.

blocked.rule: Noise on frequencies does not sanitize uncontrolled source-value or free-text labels.
Fine-grained ZIP output remains blocked by default; any future geography release requires a separately reviewed coarse public geography domain.
Patient, event and selected-subject rows may only remain protected server-side assignment objects; this registry never authorizes their release.
